name: Mixture of Quantized Experts (MoQE): Complementary Effect of Low-bit Quantization and Robustness
authors: Kim, Cho, Kim, Park, Kim, Park
problem: MoE deployment is memory-bound because ALL expert weights must be resident, even though only a few experts run per token.
mechanism: Simple weight-only quantization applied ONLY to the expert FFN weights (down to 2 bits per weight), deliberately leaving attention and the router at higher precision. No training and no special kernel work - the finding is that expert layers are structurally more robust to quantization than dense FFNs, so the standard assumption that you must protect experts does not hold.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): low-bit quantization applied only to experts 'delivers a reliable model performance while reducing the memory size significantly even without any additional training in most cases'; expert layers are 'much more robust to the quantization than conventional feedforward networks'; and MoE models with 2-bit expert weights can beat the dense model trained on the same amount of data. COMPRESSION RATIO: 2-bit expert weights (~8x on the expert tensors, which dominate MoE parameter count). QUALITY COST: 'reliable performance' / better than the data-matched dense baseline - the claim is qualitative in the abstract.
